rationale: The quantitative question (does real-call timing improve) and the qualitative question (how and why, and why hospitals differ) need both strands. A stepped introduction across four hospitals in random order lets each hospital serve as its own control while adjusting for calendar time (c1), with planning values from the intracluster correlations (c4). Real-call outcomes carry the evaluation because checklist scores are poor proxies (c2). Safety rules for unannounced simulation follow the retrieved experience (c3), and latent threats are tracked (c5).
alternatives: Parallel cluster randomised trial with two hospitals per arm (refused: two clusters per arm cannot separate programme from hospital)
Single-hospital before-after evaluation (refused: cannot separate the programme from secular change)
Simulation scores as the main outcome (refused: weak proxy for real calls)
guidelines: CONSORT extension for stepped-wedge trials, used for the quantitative strand
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial with more hospitals would give better precision but no more hospitals exist in the authority; the stepped design with a qualitative strand uses the four available hospitals best.

decision.statement: Run a four-hospital stepped mixed methods evaluation of monthly in-situ simulation for rapid response teams, with time from call to first critical intervention in real calls as the primary quantitative outcome and interviews and debrief observation as the qualitative strand, integrated by joint displays.
decision.question: How should the health authority evaluate in-situ simulation for its rapid response teams?

criteria.text: Real-call timing responds to in-situ simulation and can be measured from call records.
Call records cannot give a reliable time of the first critical intervention.

gates.requirement: Research ethics board of record approval for the multi-site study
Participation of the four hospitals' education leads
gates.evidence: Letters of participation signed between 2026-08-20 and 2026-09-05, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Funding for faculty, abstraction and interviews
gates.evidence: Grant SEF-2026-14 of 48,000 awarded on 2026-07-30, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Simulation scores as the main outcome
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c5 from retrieved records; the ethics gate has no evidence and stays unknown.

summary: Stepped mixed methods evaluation recommended; blocked until the board of record decides.
